result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [SDTMDomainTemplate]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: The structural template for an SDTM domain. twitter-card: title: >- [SDTMDomainTemplate]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: The structural template for an SDTM domain. title: >- [SDTMDomainTemplate]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: The structural template for an SDTM domain. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The structural template for an SDTM domain. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_sdtm_templates.py#L86-L257){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature SDTMDomainTemplate( domain, label, description, domain_class, repeating, variables=list(), natural_keys=list(), ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} An `SDTMDomainTemplate` describes the structure of one domain of the CDISC Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM): its label and observation class, whether it has many records per subject, the variables that form its natural key, and the specifications of its variables (as [`SDTMVariableSpec`](`pointblank.SDTMVariableSpec`) objects, in the SDTM order). Templates are obtained with [`get_sdtm_domain()`](`pointblank.get_sdtm_domain`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [domain]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The two-letter domain code, such as `"DM"`, `"AE"` or `"LB"`. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The domain label, such as `"Demographics"` or `"Adverse Events"`. [description]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A short description of what the domain holds. [domain_class]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The SDTM observation class: `"Special Purpose"`, `"Events"`, `"Interventions"` or `"Findings"`. [repeating]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Whether the domain can have more than one record per subject. Only DM, which has one record per subject, isn't repeating. [variables]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[SDTMVariableSpec]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [list()]{.doc-parameter-default} : The specifications of the domain's variables, in order. The default is an empty list. [natural_keys]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [list()]{.doc-parameter-default} : The names of the variables that together identify a record. The default is an empty list. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's look at the template for the Adverse Events (AE) domain: ::: {#d6bb03fb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb ae = pb.get_sdtm_domain("AE") print(ae.label, "|", ae.domain_class, "| repeating:", ae.repeating) print(ae.description) print(len(ae.variables), "variables") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Adverse Events | Events | repeating: True Adverse events reported during the study. 28 variables ``` ::: ::: The variables are in the `variables` list. Here are the first eight, with their type, role and core designation: ::: {#361fe163 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} for var in ae.variables[:8]: print(f"{var.name:9}{var.dtype:5}{var.role:12}{var.core}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` STUDYID Char Identifier Req DOMAIN Char Identifier Req USUBJID Char Identifier Req AESEQ Num Identifier Req AEGRPID Char Identifier Perm AEREFID Char Identifier Perm AESPID Char Identifier Perm AETERM Char Topic Req ``` ::: ::: The template's properties collect the names of the variables with a given core designation or role, and [`get_variable()`](`pointblank.SDTMDomainTemplate.get_variable`) gets the specification of one variable. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~get_sdtm_domain`) : Get the template for a domain. [](`~SDTMVariableSpec`) : The specification of a variable in the template. [](`~ADaMDatasetTemplate`) : The equivalent for ADaM datasets. ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [required_variables](#required_variables){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | The names of the required variables, in order. | | [expected_variables](#expected_variables){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | The names of the expected variables, in order. | | [identifier_variables](#identifier_variables){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | The names of the variables with the Identifier role, in order. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [required_variables]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The names of the required variables, in order. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [required_variables]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Required variables (core designation `"Req"`) must be in every dataset of the domain and can't be null. [`validate_sdtm()`](`pointblank.validate_sdtm`) adds a null check for each one, and [`validate_sdtm_structure()`](`pointblank.validate_sdtm_structure`) reports the ones that are missing. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#25949c0d .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb pb.get_sdtm_domain("DM").required_variables ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['STUDYID', 'DOMAIN', 'USUBJID', 'SUBJID', 'SITEID', 'SEX', 'ARMCD', 'ARM', 'COUNTRY'] ``` ::: ::: These are the variables that every Demographics (DM) dataset must have. This is a property, so it's used without parentheses. ### [expected_variables]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The names of the expected variables, in order. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [expected_variables]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Expected variables (core designation `"Exp"`) should be in every dataset of the domain, but their values may be null when the data wasn't collected or doesn't apply. [`validate_sdtm_structure()`](`pointblank.validate_sdtm_structure`) reports the ones that are missing when `strict=True`. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#d56faa5d .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb pb.get_sdtm_domain("DM").expected_variables ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['RFSTDTC', 'RFENDTC', 'RFXSTDTC', 'RFXENDTC', 'AGE', 'AGEU', 'RACE', 'ACTARMCD', 'ACTARM'] ``` ::: ::: For Demographics (DM), these include the reference dates (such as `RFSTDTC`), age, race and the actual arm. This is a property, so it's used without parentheses. ### [identifier_variables]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} The names of the variables with the Identifier role, in order. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [identifier_variables]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Identifier variables identify the study, the subject, the domain and the record, as with `STUDYID`, `USUBJID`, `DOMAIN` and the sequence number. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#3d289d3e .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb pb.get_sdtm_domain("AE").identifier_variables ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` ['STUDYID', 'DOMAIN', 'USUBJID', 'AESEQ', 'AEGRPID', 'AEREFID', 'AESPID'] ``` ::: ::: Besides the identifiers that all domains share, the Adverse Events (AE) template has the sequence number `AESEQ` and the optional group, reference and sponsor identifiers. This is a property, so it's used without parentheses. ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [get_variable()](#get_variable){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Get the specification of a variable. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [get_variable()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Get the specification of a variable. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_sdtm_templates.py#L221-L257){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature get_variable(name) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The variable name. This is case-sensitive, and SDTM variable names are in upper case. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [SDTMVariableSpec | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The specification of the variable, or `None` if the template has no variable with that name. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#e70f7189 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb dm = pb.get_sdtm_domain("DM") dm.get_variable("AGE") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` SDTMVariableSpec(name='AGE', label='Age', dtype='Num', role='Qualifier', required=False, max_length=None, controlled_term=None, core='Exp') ``` ::: ::: `AGE` is an expected numeric variable, so it has no maximum length. A name that isn't in the template gives `None`: ::: {#67b94500 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(dm.get_variable("age")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` None ``` ::: ::: The lookup is case-sensitive, so the lower-case name doesn't match `AGE`.
